answer: For a survey on the ripple effects of a tundra atlas, the server accepts numeric proposals from 0 to 100 and rejects others. With at least 21 proposals, it discards the 10 highest and 10 lowest, then averages the rest. Against 100 zeros, raising the result requires 11 positive submissions, costing submission effort. Honest extremes are also discarded, and a large coordinated submission can dominate.
